rows.title_full: AN ACT DESIGNATING DEATH BY LETHAL INJECTION AS THE METHOD OF CARRYING OUT CAPITAL PUNISHMENT, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 24 OF REPUBLIC ACT 7659, WHICH AMENDED ARTICLE 81 OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: Amends further Section 24 of RA 7659 by designating LETHAL INJECTION as the method of carrying out capital punishment instead of electrocution which shall be executed under the authority of the Director of [Prisons] THE BUREAU OF CORRECTIONS. Statesthat persons already sentenced by final judgment who are waiting to udnergo the death penalty by electrocution or gas poisoning shall be covered by the provisions of this Act.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A CONCLUSIVE PRESUMPTION OF LIABILITY AGAINST AN EMPLOYER WHO FAILS TO KEEP OR APPROPRIATELY PRODUCE EMPLOYMENT RECORDS FOR THE CLAIMS ARISING THEREFROM, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE ARTICLE 128 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Seeks to establish a CONCLUSIVE PRESUMPTION OF LIABILITY against the employer who fails to keep or produce the employment records for all claims, provided, that the employer shall not be liable for more than what are being claimed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 1995-09-20

rows.author: A102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MANDATORY PROFIT SHARING CLAUSE IN EVERY COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENT AND REQUIRING THE EMPLOYER TO ALLOW INSPECTION OF HIS BUSINESS BOOK FOR THIS PURPOSE, AMENDING THEREBY ARTICLE 252 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Provides for a mandatory profit sharing clause in every collective bargaining agreement and allows the CBA representative access to the business records of the employer to ensure further the right of labor to the just share in the fruits and production of any business.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07157

rows.author: A102
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE INSTITUTION OF CRIMINAL ACTION FOR AN UNFAIR LABOR PRACTICE CONSTITUTING UNION BUSTING SIMULTANEOUSLY WITH AND INDEPENDENTLY OF ANY CIVIL OR ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION ARISING FROM THE SAME UNFAIR LABOR PRACTICE, AMENDING FOR THISPURPOSE ARTICLE 247 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING THE CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS TO SELF-ORGANIZATI ON, COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AND PEACEFUL CONCERTED ACTIVITIES TO GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES WITH THE EXCEPTION OF MEMBERS OF THE MILITARY AND POLICE FORCES AND THOSE IN SECTORS PERFORMING ESSENTIAL SERVICES, AND AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 244, OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES

rows.title_full: AN ACT CRIMINALIZING RETALIATORY ACTS DIRECTED AGAINST AN EMPLOYEE WHO HAS FILED ANY COMPLAINT UNDER THE LABOR CODE OR TESTIFIED THEREUNDER, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Incorporate Article 286-A in PD No. 442, which shall read as follows: "ART. 286 - A RETALIATORY MEASURES.  IT SHALL BE UNLAWFUL FOR AN EMPLOYER TO REFUSE TO PAY IR REDUCE THE WAGES AND OTHER BENEFITS AND PRIVILEGES, DISCHARGE OR IN ANY MANNER DISCRIMINATE AGAINST ANY EMPLOYEE WHO HAS FILED ANY COMPLAINT OR INSTITUTED ANY PROCEEDING UNDER THIS CODE OR HAS TESTIFIED OR IS ABOUT TO TESTIFY IN ANY SUCH PROCEEDINGS.

rows.abstract: States that in the event of bankruptcy, INSOLVENCY ; liquidation or CLOSURE of an employer's business SALE, DISPOSIATION, or CONVEYANCE, his workers shall enjoy first preference  as regards their wages and other money claims.

rows.abstract: Provides for an integrated and continuing Health Facilities Enhancement Program which shall (1) uplift the delivery of health services to the people; (2) improve the capability of local government units in efficiently delivering health services to their local constituency; (3) rationalize and optimize the utilization and development of health facilities and services; and (4) contribute to the general enhancement and improvement of the health conditions of the community.

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION OF THE CORAL RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT AND CONSERVATION DECREE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED TWELVE HUNDRED AND NINETEEN, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Provides for the following: (1) Increase of penalty from 60 days to 6 years to 6 months to 10 years or a fine from P6,000.00 to P10,000.00 for any person gathering precious or semi-precious corals without permit; (2) Increase of penalty from 30 daysto 3 years or a fine of not less than P3,000.00 or both, to 6 months to 6 years or a fine of P6,000.00 or both for any person gathering, possessing, selling, exporting and/or using ordinary corals either in raw or processed form or exporting precious and semi-precious corals.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE MAGNA CARTA FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS
rows.abstract: Provides for the following additional benefits to public school teachers. (1) Special hardship allowance equivalent to at least [twenty-five per cent (25%)] THIRTY-FIVE PERCENT (35%) of their monthly salary.  (2) Study leave not exceeding one schoolyear after EVERY THREE [seven] years of service to PURSUE A GRADUATE SCHOOL STUDY IN EDUCATION OR ALLIED COURSES.  (3) Scholarship grant to at least TWO OF THEIR CHILDREN to any state college or university. (4) monthly longevity pay equivalent to TEN PER CENT (10%) of the monthly basic pay for each five years of continuous, efficient and meritorious service.

rows.abstract: Lowers the minimum age requirements for membership of Sangguniang Kabataan from [fifteen (15)] years old to THIRTEEN (13) years of age and increases the maximum age requirements from [twenty-one (21)] years of age to THIRTY-FIVE (35) years of age.

rows.author: A101
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 28 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'THE DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT ACT OF 1990', BY REVERTING TO THEIR FORMER NAMES THE RANK CLASSIFICATIONS IN THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL POLICE (PNP)
rows.abstract: REVERTS to their former names of the rank classifications in the Philippine National Police (PNP) which shall read as follows: Commanding General (Director General); Deputy Commanding General (Deputy Director General); General (Director); Colonel (Chief Superintendent) ; Lieutenant Colonel (Senior Superintendent) ; Major (Superintendent ); Captain (Chief Inspector) Second Lieutenant (Inspector)' Master Sergeant (Senior Police Officer III); Staff Sergeant (Senior Police Officer II); Sergeant (Senior Officer I); Patrolman III (Police Officer III); Patrolman II (Police Officer II); Patrolman I (Police Officer I)
